assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period: 17 Sep 2026 compared with 16 Sep 2026 (the immediately preceding period of equal length). The detailed analysis extends the dip window to 17-18 Sep and compares it with 10-16 Sep.

facts.text: Across 17-18 Sep the attempt success rate was 86.98% against 90.07% in the prior week (10-16 Sep). That is a fall of 3.1pp, and it is statistically significant.
The daily rate was lowest on 18 Sep at 86.66%, against a median daily rate of 89.72%. The dip window spans 17 and 18 Sep.

Kestrel Bank was the segment most concentrated in the drop. Its success rate fell 11.54pp, from 90.03% to 78.49%. The other acquirers moved by less than 0.5pp and none of those changes was significant.

Within Kestrel Bank, only card payments were hit. Debit card fell from 86.42% to 56.31% (-30.11pp), credit card from 88.64% to 59.94% (-28.71pp), and card EMI from 80.67% to 56.8% (-23.87pp). UPI, wallet and netbanking showed no significant change.
For Kestrel Bank card payments, the ACQ_TIMEOUT failure code rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures), the largest change of any failure code.

The hourly timeline shows the Kestrel card problem running about 36 hours, from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00. The worst hour was 18 Sep 02:00, with a 36.36% success rate. About 2,229 attempts were affected, with roughly 716 excess failed attempts.

The dip was spread over many hours of the day rather than one short spike. Hours 11-15 and 17-23 showed significant drops; the largest was at hour 2 (-7.26pp), though that hour was not individually significant.
The data-quality scan found no issues for the window.

response.headline: Success rates dipped because card payments routed through Kestrel Bank started failing with acquirer timeouts from about 10:00 on 17 Sep; the problem ran about 36 hours, and the overall rate fell 3.1pp from 90.07% to 86.98%.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for their incident log for 17-18 Sep and compare their outage window with the 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 window seen in the data.
hypotheses.rationale: The failures are concentrated in one acquirer and in card methods only. Failure codes point to acquirer timeouts, and UPI, wallet and netbanking through the same acquirer were unaffected.
hypotheses.text: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring side, such as an outage or connectivity degradation for card traffic, caused the timeouts and the dip.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring side, such as an outage or connectivity degradation for card traffic, caused the timeouts and the dip.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence points to one acquirer and one failure code, so the fix sits with that acquirer.
recommendations.text: Raise an incident review with Kestrel Bank to confirm the root cause of the card ACQ_TIMEOUT spike and get a written timeline.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Kestrel Bank card payments, the ACQ_TIMEOUT failure code rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
recommendations.rationale: The problem ran about 36 hours before ending; faster detection and rerouting would limit the lost attempts.
recommendations.text: Set up an hourly alert on card success rate and ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts by acquirer, and consider automatic failover of card traffic to other acquirers when timeouts spike.
